title: SC-MT011-SessionToolGate

scope.summary:
GOAL: Build the SessionToolGate - Handshake's OWN vendor-agnostic tool-call interception point for agent sessions. OPERATOR FRAMING (2026-07-22): Handshake is a model/vendor-agnostic engine that WRAPS whatever runs the model (today: vendor CLIs, chosen only because Anthropic subscription plans block direct API use); the wrapper - not the vendor harness - must be able to see, allow, deny, and STOP any tool call a session's model attempts. Today that power is fragmented per transport: the Claude lane trusts the vendor's own permission flags (allowedTools/permission-mode mapping, CS MT-021), the Codex lane bridges app-server approval requests (CX MT-044), and the ACP lane bridges session/request_permission (AP MT-063). This MT creates the single Handshake-owned policy point all three (and every future vendor lane) route through, so tool-call governance is a Dexterity capability, not a vendor feature.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New module src/backend/handshake_core/src/agent_sessions/tool_gate.rs (plus a policy submodule if size warrants): typed ToolCallRequest { session_id, parent_session_id, lane_kind, tool_name, tool_class (FileRead|FileWrite|Exec|Network|HandshakePrimitive|Unknown), args_digest (hash, never raw secrets), workspace_scope, requested_at }; typed ToolGateDecision { Allow, Deny(reason), AskOperator(prompt_ref), StopSession(reason) }; a SessionToolGate service evaluating ordered policy rules (per-role tool_policy from RO MT-081, per-session overrides, model-to-model policy MM MT-106 for child sessions, global denylist) with DENY-BY-DEFAULT for Unknown tool classes; decision + latency ledgered and FR-evented per RD MT-161 kinds; AskOperator wired through the existing consent surface (ConsentGate pattern, model_runtime/cloud/consent_gate.rs) with deny-on-timeout.

TRANSPORT BINDING SPEC (integration obligations - the adapters bind to this gate; this MT delivers the gate + the binding seams + at least the Claude binding live): (1) CLAUDE LANE: serve the gate as the CLI's permission prompt tool - launch preset gains --permission-prompt-tool pointing at a Handshake-served MCP tool (mcp/gate.rs GatedMcpClient server-side pattern) so EVERY gated tool call in the Claude CLI asks Handshake for permission; denial returns the vendor-native refusal shape; this supersedes flag-only trust from CS MT-021 (allowedTools remains a coarse pre-filter only). (2) CODEX LANE: CX MT-044's approval bridge routes item/commandExecution/requestApproval + item/fileChange/requestApproval through SessionToolGate instead of a bespoke path. (3) ACP LANE: AP MT-063's session/request_permission handler routes through SessionToolGate. (4) FUTURE LANES: the gate trait is the documented seam a new vendor adapter must implement to be admitted to production_factory.

STOP SEMANTICS: StopSession triggers the supervisor's graceful-stop ladder (SC MT-005) and records a typed terminal reason; Deny never kills the session (model continues, tool refused).

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read agent_sessions module state from MT-001..010 (session model, capabilities, supervisor, API) and mcp/gate.rs + consent_gate.rs for the incumbent gating patterns.
2. Define ToolCallRequest/ToolGateDecision/ToolClass types + serde; classification table mapping known vendor tool names (Bash/Read/Write/Edit etc. for Claude; command_execution/file_change for Codex; ACP terminal/fs services) to ToolClass - table is data, not code, so new vendors extend without recompiling classification logic.
3. Implement SessionToolGate policy evaluation: ordered sources (global denylist > MM MT-106 child policy > role tool_policy RO MT-081 > session overrides > class defaults), deny-by-default for Unknown; every decision writes a ledger row + FR event (RD MT-161/162 seams) with request digest and rule that fired.
4. Implement AskOperator: consent prompt surfaced via the existing consent flow; configurable timeout; timeout=Deny; decision cached per (session, tool_name, args_digest) when the operator marks 'remember for this session'.
5. Implement StopSession wiring to SC MT-005 supervisor graceful stop with typed reason.
6. Bind the Claude lane live: extend the interactive launch preset with --permission-prompt-tool served by a Handshake MCP endpoint backed by SessionToolGate; prove a gated Bash call is denied by Handshake policy while an allowed Read passes.
7. Expose the binding trait + docs for CX MT-044 / AP MT-063 to consume (their contracts already bridge approvals; this MT provides the shared evaluator they call).
8. Unit + integration tests incl. deny-by-default, precedence order, timeout-deny, stop ladder, ledger completeness.
forbidden_paths: src/frontend/** (no GUI in this MT; consent surfaces reuse existing flows)
acceptance_criteria: SessionToolGate evaluates ToolCallRequest to Allow/Deny/AskOperator/StopSession with deny-by-default for Unknown tool classes; precedence order (global denylist > child policy > role policy > session overrides > class defaults) is proven by tests.
Every decision produces a ledger row and FR event with the rule that fired; a missing ledger write fails the decision closed (Deny).

Claude lane binding live: a session launched with the interactive preset routes gated tool calls through --permission-prompt-tool to Handshake; a policy-denied Bash call is refused inside the live CLI session while an allowed Read proceeds.
AskOperator times out to Deny; 'remember for session' caching works and is ledgered.
StopSession invokes the SC MT-005 graceful-stop ladder and records a typed terminal reason.
The gate trait + classification table are documented as the mandatory seam for future vendor lanes; CX MT-044 and AP MT-063 integration points compile against the shared evaluator.
No vendor name appears in gate types, schema ids, or policy vocabulary (vendor names live only in the per-lane classification table data).
proof_targets: cargo test -p handshake_core session_tool_gate --nocapture 2>&1 | grep -E 'test result: ok'
expected_tests: live Claude permission-prompt-tool round trip (ignored/typed-blocker when CLI absent)
implementation_notes: OPERATOR FRAMING 2026-07-22: Handshake is the vendor-agnostic engine wrapping the model transport; vendor harness permission systems are pre-filters at most - the Handshake gate is authoritative. This MT exists because the earlier per-transport MTs (CS MT-021 flag mapping, CX MT-044 approval bridge, AP MT-063 permission bridge) each leaned on the vendor surface; they now converge on this shared evaluator.

Claude --permission-prompt-tool is the documented mechanism for delegating permission decisions to the controller (verified in the 2026-07-21 research pass); the Handshake-served MCP tool returns the CLI's expected allow/deny payload shape.
args_digest: hash + bounded redacted preview only; never persist raw tool arguments that may carry secrets (typed-allowlist discipline).
Classification table ships as data (const table or config) keyed by (lane_kind, tool_name) so adding GPT/open-source lanes is a data change.

Do not edit MT-021/044/063 contracts; their integration duty is expressed here and in the index; implementers of those MTs read this contract via depends_on direction at activation (packet-level ordering note in _MT_INDEX.json).

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend policy engine; operator consent prompts reuse the existing consent surface, and gate decisions surface in the RD MT-166 audit pane.

target_entries: Dexterity tool gate: how Handshake allows/denies/stops model tool calls across all lanes

risk_if_missed: Tool-call governance stays fragmented per vendor; Handshake cannot claim to sandbox/stop model actions independently of vendor harness behavior - the core engine promise of the wrapper is unmet.

risks: RISK-1: A vendor lane bypasses the gate (tool calls execute vendor-side without asking Handshake), making the gate decorative.
RISK-2: Unknown/new vendor tool names default to Allow, silently widening the sandbox.
RISK-3: Raw tool arguments (secrets, file contents) get persisted in ledger rows.
RISK-4: AskOperator prompts block sessions indefinitely or fail open on timeout.
RISK-5: StopSession leaves the child process or its tool subprocesses alive.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Per-lane binding proof required (Claude live in this MT; CX/AP assert shared-evaluator usage in their contract suites); a lane without a gate binding is not admitted to production_factory.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Deny-by-default for Unknown tool classes, proven by test; classification table changes require a test row.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): args_digest = hash + bounded redacted preview; ledger schema has no raw-args column; test asserts absence.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Consent timeout is mandatory config with deny-on-timeout; proven by test.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): StopSession routes through the SC MT-005 tree-kill ladder with ledger STOP row; proof asserts no surviving descendants.

research_provenance.source: Operator vendor-agnostic-engine directive 2026-07-22; verified per-transport gating state (CS MT-021 flag mapping, CX MT-044 approvals, AP MT-063 permissions); Claude --permission-prompt-tool mechanism from 2026-07-21 research pass; mcp/gate.rs + consent_gate.rs incumbent patterns.
